transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-15
Time: 15:00 UTC (60 min calendar slot; recorded)
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Leo Tran (Redwood SE); Sam Ortiz (CTO - Apollo Retail), Priya Rao (Lead ML Eng), Derek Chu (Backend Eng), Lina Gomez (PM)

Summary: Quick scoping call to align on proof-of-concept (POC) objectives for an Inventory Assistant feature. Focus areas: SDK integration (OpenAI-compatible endpoints), tool/function calling for real-time inventory queries, structured JSON output for downstream systems, workload sizing and benchmark plan, timeline and success criteria.

Topics covered: success criteria, latency / throughput targets, monthly token estimates, sample prompts and structured outputs, security/VPC options, benchmark plan and timeline, next steps for SOW and test datasets.

Action items (also in metadata): listed below.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick agenda — align on POC goals, talk integration surface (SDK vs raw HTTP), get workloads for benchmarking, and set a 4-week plan. Sam, do you want to start with high-level ask?
[00:32] Sam Ortiz (Apollo CTO): Yeah hi thanks. We're building an Inventory Assistant inside our retailer portal. primary use: agents ask natural language queries like "how many of sku 1234 across east region" and get structured replies plus links to actions. We need it to call our inventory service and sometimes kick off reorders.
[01:05] Priya Rao (Lead ML Eng): Our big constraints are: sub-300ms median token latency on common queries, p95 under 700ms ideally, and the JSON output needs to be strict schema so downstream ETL doesn't break. Also we need to validate hallucination rates — less than 1% critical factual errors on inventory numbers.
[01:42] Maya Singh (Redwood SE): Got it. For the latency goals we'll look at model choice + routing policies. We can run tests on our hosted endpoints first, and if you need guaranteed tails we can spin a dedicated pool. For JSON schema enforcement we support structured output and also function/tool calling to let your service own the truth.
[02:18] Derek Chu (Apollo Eng): Quick question — we already use an OpenAI-compatible wrapper internally. can we just point it to that? or do we have to refactor?
[02:40] Leo Tran (Redwood SE): You can use OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Redwood's API accepts ChatCompletion-style payloads and also has a lightweight SDK that mirrors openai-python patterns. Tool calling is supported in the same compatibility layer, though our SDK has helpers to register endpoint URLs and handle retries and webhook callbacks.
[03:15] Lina Gomez (PM): Timeline wise, we want to see a working flow in a dash in about 4 weeks. First week: integration + sample data; second week: benchmark pass; week 3: iterate on schema and fallbacks; week 4: finalize runbook and exec demo. Is that feasible?
[03:46] Maya Singh (Redwood SE): Yes that's reasonable for a constrained POC. We'll aim for a 4-week pilot. We'll need your sample prompt set, expected QPS/concurrency, and a representative token distribution.
[04:10] Priya Rao: For traffic, typical interactive queries are 20–80 tokens input, 40–180 tokens output. Peak concurrency for a pilot is about 50 QPS but sustained avg is closer to 8–12 QPS. Monthly tokens estimate is ~15M tokens for pilot scope.
[04:48] Jordan Park: Perfect, that helps size things. For costs we'll model hosted first; if the p95 or throughput doesn't meet your SLOs we can propose dedicated nodes and estimated reserved capacity.
[05:12] Sam Ortiz: On security — how do you handle our data? we need SOC2, SSO, RBAC, and option for VPC peering or private deployment down the road.
[05:36] Maya Singh: Redwood has SOC2 Type II in our docs — we'll share the pack. For the POC we can do VPC peering to a private subnet and ensure keys are handled via KMS. For on-prem or air-gapped there's a private deployment option but that's more involved and out of scope for a 4-week POC.
[06:02] Derek Chu: What about data retention — we need logs for audit but can't retain customer PII in training data.
[06:18] Maya Singh: We support configurable retention and redact patterns. Hosted mode can be configured to not use data for model training and to purge logs after X days based on policy. We'll include retention controls in the SOW.
[06:44] Priya Rao: For hallucination checks — we already have an internal test harness that asserts numbers against our canonical DB for a test corpus. can Redwood's test harness call our database or do we need to feed ground-truth labels?
[07:05] Leo Tran: Two options — you can either allow function/tool calling where the model returns an intent and we route to your inventory API for the final numeric answer, or you can let the model produce JSON and we run an evaluation job that compares the JSON to ground-truth you supply. Function calling is preferable to fully eliminate hallucination for numeric fields.
[07:35] Sam Ortiz: Sounds like function calling + strict schema is the best approach. We also want audit logs whenever the model triggers a reorder action.
[07:50] Maya Singh: We record request/response at token level in trace logs and can attach metadata for audit. For reorders we recommend a two-step flow: model suggests reorder intent, a human or automated rule confirms, then the actual reorder API is called. Redwood can surface those traces in the Console.
[08:20] Lina Gomez: Ok let's talk benchmarks. We want to compare your hosted endpoint vs our current OpenAI wrapper and evaluate any dedicated config if needed. The benchmark should measure latency distribution, cost per 1k tokens, and correctness on the prompt set.
[08:46] Jordan Park: We'll prepare a benchmark script that hits both endpoints with identical prompt payloads and captures token counts, latencies, and structured-output parsing success. Maya, can you outline what we'll need from Apollo?
[09:06] Maya Singh: Sure: (1) provide 200–300 representative prompts (both short and long queries), (2) provide expected schema for JSON outputs, (3) provide a ground-truth mapping for a subset (say 100 examples) for correctness checks, (4) share concurrency/traffic profile and an env for function-calling endpoints (staging inventory API).
[09:36] Priya Rao: We'll compile a prompt set and ground truth; can do 150 canonical queries this week and expand to 300 by next Wed. We can provide a staging API with a token-limited key.
[09:58] Derek Chu: On the SDK do you have examples for function registration? we want to avoid building glue code.
[10:12] Leo Tran: Yes, our SDK has a simple decorator to register tool endpoints and a webhook handshake to verify responses. We also export a lightweight shim to convert legacy OpenAI function-call format into calls we do internally. We'll include code samples in the repo we share.
[10:40] Maya Singh: Also note that our OpenAI-compatible path supports both chat completions and the newer function calling - we try to preserve signature compatibility so fewer changes on your side. For performance it's sometimes better to use Redwood-native streaming SDK which reduces cold start latency on the first token.
[11:08] Sam Ortiz: We care about cold starts — our UI cannot wait multiple seconds on first query. What's the realistic cold start improvement?
[11:22] Maya Singh: With hosted warm pools, first token can be under 200ms for smaller models; large models vary. If cold starts are an issue at scale, Dedicated with prewarmed instances is recommended. We'll measure cold/warm in benchmarks.
[11:44] Priya Rao: Regarding model choice — do you expose quantized variants? our primary goal is correctness but cost matters.
[11:56] Jordan Park: Yes, we have quantized variants and hardware-aware kernel selection. For POC we'll run 2–3 model variants (a small LLM for quick queries, a mid-sized one for better reasoning, and a quantized variant) to see the cost/latency/correctness tradeoffs.
[12:20] Lina Gomez: For success criteria, let's be explicit: 1) p95 latency ≤700ms on pilot traffic, 2) correctness on numeric inventory fields ≥99% vs ground truth, 3) structured JSON outputs pass schema validation ≥98% parsing success, 4) integration done end-to-end including function call to staging inventory API.
[12:50] Jordan Park: Sounds good, we can commit to those targets for the POC. If we can't meet p95 with hosted we'll propose dedicated sizing and expected pricing impact.
[13:10] Priya Rao: How do we validate cost? we need a cost per 1M tokens estimate for each model variant plus a forecast for monthly run if we scaled to prod.
[13:30] Jordan Park: We'll run the benchmark and produce a cost model: tokens per request x cost per model x QPS. We'll include a comparison to your current OpenAI spend.
[13:50] Derek Chu: In terms of infra, what network changes are needed for VPC peering? we don't want to open public endpoints.
[14:05] Maya Singh: For VPC peering we'll provide the required CIDR ranges and a peering setup doc. For the POC we can also use a tunneled staging API with IP allowlist. We'll share the network checklist.
[14:30] Sam Ortiz: Are there any limitations around function calling concurrency like rate limits?
[14:42] Leo Tran: Rate limits exist but are configurable for pilot. For production we'll size dedicated pools. For the benchmark we'll emulate your concurrency profile to see if any throttles happen.
[15:00] Lina Gomez: Ok let's lock down dates. Jordan you said you'll send SOW by Friday?
[15:10] Jordan Park: Yes, I'll send draft SOW and pricing tiers by 2025-10-17. Maya will send the benchmark harness and sample scripts by 10-20. We propose kickoff benchmark run the week of 10/20 with an initial run on 10/22.
[15:30] Priya Rao: We'll have the initial prompt set and staging API ready by 10/17. Derek will coordinate infra access.
[16:00] Derek Chu: I'll open a ticket with our infra team and send contact details by 10/18.
[16:20] Maya Singh: For the technical approach to validation, we'll run three phases: 1) compatibility check (OpenAI-compat SDK + function calling), 2) performance benchmark (latency/cost/throughput across variants), 3) correctness sweep (run ground-truth compares and regression tests). We'll share a results template so we can quickly see which variant meets the SLOs.
[16:56] Sam Ortiz: If you can map out how we'd move from hosted POC to Dedicated, that'd be useful — especially cost delta and what triggers that change.
[17:10] Jordan Park: Absolutely — we'll include a migration/runbook section in the SOW that shows thresholds where dedicated is recommended (e.g., sustained p95 breaches or >X QPS). We'll include estimated reserved capacity costs.
[17:38] Priya Rao: A couple of edge cases — sometimes the model returns partial JSON or unparsable strings, do you have fallback parsing or repair heuristics?
[17:56] Maya Singh: Yes we have an auto-repair layer that can attempt to reparse, and we can run a quick second-shot completion to fix malformed JSON. But for numeric inventory fields we prefer function-call-confirm flows to avoid repairs.
[18:20] Lina Gomez: Ok great. Anything else from Redwood side?
[18:32] Leo Tran: We'll also include code samples for our SDK in Node/Python and an example of registering a function for inventory lookup with signature and response schema.
[18:48] Sam Ortiz: Good. For procurement, we'll need your standard MSA and a short SOW addendum for the pilot.
[19:05] Jordan Park: We'll attach the MSA template and POC SOW to the follow-up.
[19:20] Priya Rao: On metrics — can Redwood export token-level traces so we can correlate particular prompts with DB queries?
[19:35] Maya Singh: Yes, the Console and trace export supports token-level traces and request metadata; we'll provide a CSV/JSON export format.
[19:50] Derek Chu: For the benchmark harness — will the script handle streaming outputs and measure first-byte latency?
[20:05] Maya Singh: The harness will capture streaming first-token latency and full-response latency, and will compute median/p90/p95 stats.
[20:28] Jordan Park: All right, recap of next steps: Jordan send SOW by 10/17; Maya send benchmark harness and SDK samples by 10/20; Apollo provide prompt set and staging API credentials by 10/17; benchmark kickoff 10/22. We'll aim to complete the 4-week POC by 11/12.
[20:55] Sam Ortiz: That works. Thank you everyone.
[21:05] Lina Gomez: Thanks, talk soon.

Appendix - Notes on evaluation metrics (in call):
- Latency: median and p95 targets, measure cold vs warm token latency
- Cost: cost per 1M tokens per model variant, plus estimated monthly in pilot and projected prod
- Correctness: numeric match rate against DB; hallucination <1% for critical fields
- Parsing: structured JSON schema pass rate

References shared during call:
- Redwood SOW template (link to repo)
- Benchmark harness (will be shared by Maya via repo link)
- Apollo staging API details (to be provided by Derek)

End of transcript.
